  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  April 3, 2023

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Rebecca Perez, Community Services Director

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Discussion of the 2023 Annual Workplan

SUMMARY
This is the Annual Workplan developed by the Community Services Commission and is
intended for the 2023 calendar year. The Community Services Commission approved the
2023 Workplan on December 5, 2022, which was originally carried over from the 2022
Annual Workplan. The 2022 Annual Workplan was approved by the City Council during
the September 6, 2022 City Council meeting.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.

Purpose of the Annual Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2023. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.

  4-A
 APPROVED ANNUAL WORKPLAN 2023
The 2023 Workplan sets forth five priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore.

1. Create New Innovative Programs and Services to Engage the Entire Community
  a. Develop and implement pop-up events or host an information booth at
  events publicizing all transportation services offered in the City
  b. Collaborate with businesses/organizations in order to offer additional social
  services to older adults
  i. For example: Collaborating with businesses offering tracking
  devices/systems for older adults with memory related health issues
  c. Develop an internship program for youth to assist with translation services

2. Connect the Entire Community to Enhance Quality of Life
  a. Continue to support health services by partnering with health service
  providers
  i. Examples include: Herald Christian and USC School of Pharmacy
  b. Develop and implement a Community Services Department Day advertising
  all programs, events and services offered by the Community Services Department
  c. Connect all geographic areas of the City
  i. Examples include: Hosting events and programs in the South San Gabriel
  area and various other neighborhoods

3. Embrace and Celebrate Community Diversity
  a. Propose a Moon Festival to be held in the Mission District; due to the potential
  budget impact of this event, the proposal would need to be brought forward to
  the City Council for implementation
  b. Partner and collaborate with various cultural and interfaith organizations to
  assist in the development and implementation of events and services
  i. Examples include: Partnering with the HEAR Commission, Native American
  Community and interfaith groups

4. Plan and Create New and Enhanced Open Spaces, Parks and Community Facilities
  a. Enhance current park spaces

  4-A
   i. Examples include: Enhancement of Smith Park and updating Community
  Services facilities
  b. Seek additional park spaces and amenities
  i. Examples include: Dog area and rubberized running trail

5. Develop Innovative Resources and Tools to Achieve our Mission
  a. Collect survey data with targeted questions to improve, enhance and seek
  additional services as needed
  b. Identify community leaders and organizations to offer additional resources
  c. Utilize social platforms to reach various audiences
  i. For example: Utilizing WeChat social media
  d. Cross promote programs through various City Departments
  i. For example: utilize Police Department’s Neighborhood Watch to
  disseminate information

FISCAL IMPACT
Should the following items be included in the Annual Workplan, staff and the Commission
recognize that there may be fiscal impacts:
• Develop and implement a Community Services Department Day advertising all
programs, events and services offered by the Community Services Department
• Propose a Moon Festival to be held in the Mission District
• Enhance current park spaces
• Seek additional park spaces and amenities

Once staff and the Commission determine the associated cost for these items, should they
not fall within the existing department budget, staff will present the items to the City
Council at a later date for possible budgetary allocation, review and approval.

recommended that the Commission survey residents at various departmental events to
gain analytical data and better inform the community about services, activities and events
the Community Services Department offers. Below are a list proposed questions and the
current survey evaluating the communication efforts for the commission to consider.

  5. Are you aware of the transportation resources offered by the city?

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  April 3, 2023

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Community Services Department Staff

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Monthly Department Report

Youth Programs
All City Pentathlon – The All-City Pentathlon took place on Saturday, March 25 at
Jefferson Middle School. Approximately 70 San Gabriel Unified School District students
from Coolidge, McKinley, Roosevelt, Washington and Wilson Elementary Schools, and
Jefferson Middle School took place in the track and field events. The events included a 50
and 200 meter dash, standing and running long jump, and a softball toss. Over 200
spectators attended this event to cheer on student athletes. Community Services staff did
a great job in preparing the student athletes for competition.

Older Adults
Social Bingo – Social Bingo will take place Thursday, April 20 at the Adult Recreation
Center. Registration is recommended by calling the Community Services Department and
walk-ins are welcome.
Special Senior Luncheon – On Wednesday, March 15 the Adult Recreation Center hosted
a St. Patrick’s Day themed luncheon with over 75 participants in attendance. On
Wednesday, April 19 the Adult Recreation Center will host a Spring Celebration themed
luncheon, along with raffle prizes. Registration is available by calling the Community
Services Office.

Special Events
78th Annual Spring Celebration – The 78th Annual Spring Celebration will take place on
Saturday, April 8 from 7:00am to 11:00am. In partnership with the Kiwanis Club of San Gabriel,
the event will feature a pancake breakfast, egg hunt, pancake races, coloring contest, bubble
fun zone and photos with Mr. Bunny.
